data.narrative:
Seurat Technologies, a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by James DeMuth, has raised $178M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies—Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—alongside one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $178M total raised proxy, yielding $303M. Peer-median analysis across the three robotics comparables produces a $1.0B median valuation, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The divergence between methods reflects uncertainty in whether Seurat commands peer-equivalent multiples or remains below the cohort median.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $257M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $651M. This spread reflects two material uncertainties: first, Seurat's relative competitive positioning within an active peer set where valuations vary by 60% ($1.0B–$1.6B); second, whether the $178M raised-to-date should be discounted as insufficient signal of market expectations at Series C close. A valuation toward the upper quartile ($850M–$1.0B) would imply Seurat achieves near-peer parity; a position at $400M–$650M would indicate a modest discount to median peers.
